headline: FICO, the company behind the widely used credit score, is cutting about 15% of its workforce in a restructuring it links to AI.
score_reason: Company statement to Reuters; number of jobs is a Reuters estimate.
importance_line: Roughly 570 people may lose jobs, based on Reuters's reading of last year's headcount, and the cut comes while FICO's shares have fallen about 58% this year, so AI is not the only pressure.
summary: Reuters reports, as relayed by CNA, that Fair Isaac (FICO) said the cut is part of a broader restructuring and AI integration meant to simplify its structure; the company did not say how many staff, which on its September 2025 headcount of 3,811 would mean about 570 people. It expects about $27 million in pre-tax charges in the fourth quarter of its 2026 fiscal year, mostly severance, and its shares are down about 58% this year after US regulators moved to let lenders use the rival VantageScore in mortgage lending.
notes: Reuters page blocked; read the Reuters text carried by CNA. url is the Reuters link from the pool.
